title: Good scoring / good rubrics shortlist
notes: Refocused Method Lab screen: scoring quality & rubrics (not hiring apps). From 1944 unique papers → 162 method-strong → top 10 + 5 craft adjacent.

papers.title: From Rubrics to Reliable Scores: Evidence-Grounded Text Evaluation with LLM Judges
papers.summary: RULERS compiles natural-language rubrics into executable, versioned criteria with evidence-anchored scoring and scale calibration.
papers.summarySimple: Turns scoring rubrics into locked, executable checklists with evidence and calibrated scores.

impact.forTech: Build a rubric compiler + evidence-anchored scorer: version criteria, verify cited evidence, calibrate score scales.
impact.forBusiness: Replace holistic AI scores with auditable, versioned rubrics buyers can trust.

papers.title: Autorubric: Unifying Rubric-based LLM Evaluation
papers.summary: Unifies rubric design, ensemble judging, few-shot calibration, bias mitigations, and psychometric reliability metrics into one framework.
papers.summarySimple: One playbook for building reliable rubric-based AI graders.

impact.forTech: Ship a scoring platform with per-criterion judges, ensembles, calibration sets, and kappa/QWK reporting.
impact.forBusiness: Turns scattered eval tricks into a repeatable scoring product.

papers.title: PReMISE: Policy Rubrics as Measurement Specifications for LLM Judges
papers.summary: Frames rubrics as measurement specifications so vague quality language becomes scoreable, policy-grade criteria.
papers.summarySimple: Makes fuzzy scoring policies into clear, measurable rubric specs.

impact.forTech: Authoring UX that compiles policy language into measurable rubric items before any judge runs.
impact.forBusiness: Stops 'vibes scoring'—buyers get criteria they can audit.

papers.title: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement
papers.summary: Selective evaluation with confidence estimation and cascaded judges that guarantee a target human-agreement level.
papers.summarySimple: Only auto-scores when confident; otherwise escalates to a stronger judge or human.

impact.forTech: Add selective scoring + escalation gates with coverage vs agreement knobs.
impact.forBusiness: High-stakes scoring with a reliability SLA, not blind automation.

papers.title: Diagnosing the Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge via Item Response Theory
papers.summary: Applies Item Response Theory to diagnose whether LLM judges behave as stable measurement instruments.
papers.summarySimple: Uses psychometrics to test if an AI judge is a trustworthy measuring tool.

impact.forTech: Add IRT dashboards for judge ability, item difficulty, and score validity checks.
impact.forBusiness: Prove scores measure the intended trait—not just rater agreement.

papers.title: Evaluating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
papers.summary: Defines and measures scoring biases from rubric order, score IDs, and reference-answer prompts.
papers.summarySimple: Shows how tiny prompt/rubric tweaks quietly change AI scores.

impact.forTech: Build a scoring-bias audit suite that perturbs rubrics/IDs/references and reports score drift.
impact.forBusiness: Hardens scorecards before they ship to production.

papers.title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias
papers.summary: Large-scale study showing common agreement metrics can look good while validity fails; pushes better protocols.
papers.summarySimple: Warns that consistent AI scores can still be wrong about what they claim to measure.

impact.forTech: Require reliability+validity test packs before promoting a scoring model.
impact.forBusiness: Avoid shipping 'reliable' scores that do not measure the real outcome.

papers.title: From Holistic Evaluation to Structured Criteria: Rubrics Across the Evolving LLM Landscape
papers.summary: Survey of the field's shift from scalar holistic scores to structured, verifiable rubric criteria.
papers.summarySimple: Maps why good scoring moved from one overall score to clear multi-criteria rubrics.

impact.forTech: Design vocabulary and architecture: analytic dimensions, checklist items, meta-eval layers.
impact.forBusiness: Explains the category story: structured rubrics beat vibes scores.

papers.title: JudgmentBench: Comparing Rubric and Preference Evaluation for Quality Assessment
papers.summary: Benchmark comparing rubric-based scoring vs preference judging for quality assessment.
papers.summarySimple: Tests when rubric scores beat pairwise 'which is better' judgments.

impact.forTech: Support both rubric and preference modes with an A/B meta-eval harness.
impact.forBusiness: Pick the right scoring mode per task instead of one default.

papers.title: RubricEval: A Rubric-Level Meta-Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Judges in Instruction Following
papers.summary: Criterion-level meta-evaluation: checks whether judges correctly evaluate each rubric item.
papers.summarySimple: Checks if the AI grader got each rubric line right—not just the final score.

impact.forTech: Add criterion-level goldens and meta-eval loops for every rubric dimension.
impact.forBusiness: Catches silent criterion failures that overall scores hide.

papers.title: Prometheus: Inducing Fine-grained Evaluation Capability in Language Models
papers.summary: Open fine-grained rubric judges as an alternative to proprietary GPT judges.
papers.summarySimple: Open fine-grained rubric judges as an alternative to proprietary GPT judges.

impact.forTech: Useful scoring-craft reference for rubric authoring, calibration, or meta-eval.
impact.forBusiness: Strengthens scoring quality without a domain costume.
